title: Losing Streak May Continue For Singapore Stock Market

text:
Losing Streak May Continue For Singapore Stock Market November 12, 2018, 06:59:00 PM EDT By RTTNews Shutterstock photo
( RTTNews.com ) - The Singapore stock market has finished lower in consecutive trading days, surrendering more than 20 points or 0.7 percent along the way. The Straits Times Index now rests just beneath the 3,070-point plateau and it's likely to take further damage on Tuesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is soft, with weakness expected among the technology stocks and oil companies. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourse are expected to follow suit.
The STI finished modestly lower on Monday following losses from the financial shares and the property stocks, while the industrials and plantations were mixed.
For the day, the index shed 9.82 points or 0.32 percent to finish at 3,068.15 after trading between 3,059.32 and 3,089.82. Volume was 1.57 billion shares worth 809 million Singapore dollars. There were 236 decliners and 145 gainers.
Among the actives, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding plummeted 2.31 percent, while Golden Agri-Resources plunged 2.00 percent, SembCorp Industries soared 1.90 percent, SingTel tumbled 1.61 percent, Thai Beverage skidded 1.52 percent, Comfort DelGro spiked 1.38 percent, Genting Singapore dropped 1.05 percent, Keppel Corp climbed 0.97 percent, Wilmar International jumped 0.95 percent, DBS Group shed 0.93 percent, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation lost 0.79 percent, United Overseas Bank fell 0.69 percent, CapitaLand dipped 0.64 percent, CapitaLand Commercial Trust was down 0.59 percent, Ascendas REIT added 0.39 percent and Hutchison Port Holdings and CapitaLand Mall Trust were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as stocks moved sharply lower on Monday, extending losses from the previous session.
The Dow plunged 602.12 points or 2.32 percent to 25,387.18, while the NASDAQ dropped 206.03 points or 2.78 percent to 7,200.87 and the S&P fell 54.79 points or 1.97 percent to 2,726.22.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple ( AAPL ) and General Electric (GE) weighed on the markets, while concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates also contributed to the sell-off.
Light trading activity may have exaggerated the downward move, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks were closed in observance of Veterans Day.
Crude oil shook off early gains on Monday to end lower for the 11th straight session on oversupply concerns. Crude oil futures for December, which rose to $61.28 earlier in the session, settled lower by $0.26 or 0.4 percent at $59.93 a barrel, the lowest settlement since February.
